1.explanation:
1. audits/byte-efficiency/large-javascript-libraries-test.js: This test covers the specific audit that produces the “Library” table with its “Transfer Size” values; it will need updating when the displayValue logic changes to include ".0" for whole-number sizes.
2. audits/byte-efficiency/byte-efficiency-audit-test.js & its __snapshots__: These capture generic byte-efficiency audit outputs (including size formatting) and will need their expected snapshots updated to reflect the always-show-decimal behavior.
3. report/html/renderer/util-test.js: The formatBytes utility under test here is responsible for converting raw byte counts into human-readable strings (e.g. "KiB"); modifying it to always show one decimal will require corresponding test adjustments.
4. report/html/renderer/details-renderer-test.js: DetailsRenderer applies formatBytes to build the table cells; its tests verify how values render in the UI, so they must be updated to expect the trailing ".0".
5. lib/i18n/i18n-test.js: The underlying i18n number-formatting options determine decimal display; ensuring a minimum of one decimal place interacts with these options, so tests here should be reviewed and updated as needed.
1.bug_scenario: In the “Replace unnecessarily large JavaScript libraries” audit (under Byte Efficiency), the “Transfer Size” column shows sizes like “70.4 KiB”, “2.8 KiB” and “20.4 KiB” but omits the decimal place for round numbers, rendering “18 KiB” instead of “18.0 KiB”. Because the trailing “.0” is dropped, the numeric columns don’t line up, making it harder for low-vision users to compare values at a glance.
